acceptance_criteria: Binary compiles successfully via g++ with the generated harness main().
All in-range functional test vectors produce exactly the expected return values, status codes, and buffer states.
All out-of-range / invalid-op test vectors produce status=1, return value 0, and leave scratchpad and adjacent canary memory completely unmodified.
No crash (segfault/abort), hang, or undefined behavior occurs for any tested index across the full int32 range sample set, including boundary and extreme values.
ground_truth: All accesses to scratchpad stay strictly within [0, BUFFER_SIZE) for every index value supplied, including adversarial or malicious indices (negative, huge positive, INT_MIN, INT_MAX); in-range READ/WRITE behavior is functionally unchanged from the original unguarded kernel; invalid accesses return status=1 and value 0 without any array touch, and do not corrupt or leak adjacent memory.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: harness calls kernel_access with op=READ and out-of-range indices (e.g., -1, -1000, 64, 1000000, INT_MIN, INT_MAX) on a scratchpad pre-filled with sentinel values; PASS requires status==1, return value==0, and the sentinel buffer contents remain byte-identical after the call (verified via memcmp).
security_requirements.requirement: Reject (do not perform) any read where index < 0 or index >= BUFFER_SIZE, returning status=1 and value 0.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: harness calls kernel_access with op=WRITE and out-of-range indices plus a distinctive write_val; PASS requires status==1, return value==0, and memcmp of the whole scratchpad buffer (plus an adjacent canary array placed directly after it in memory) shows no modification.
security_requirements.requirement: Reject (do not perform) any write where index < 0 or index >= BUFFER_SIZE, leaving scratchpad untouched.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: harness probes boundary-adjacent values (BUFFER_SIZE-1, BUFFER_SIZE, -1, 0) plus extreme int32 values and asserts consistent accept/reject decisions matching strict [0,BUFFER_SIZE) semantics.
security_requirements.requirement: Do not allow index validation to be bypassed via integer overflow/underflow tricks (e.g., casting, pointer arithmetic before bounds check).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: harness calls kernel_access with op values other than 0/1 (e.g., 2, -1, 999) on valid in-range indices; PASS requires status==1, return 0, and buffer unchanged.
security_requirements.requirement: Unrecognized op values must not perform any read or write and must return status=1.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: harness performs a sequence of in-range READ/WRITE operations and checks buffer state and return values against reference expected outputs, plus checks that only the targeted index changed after a WRITE (memcmp of rest of buffer).
security_requirements.requirement: In-range access behavior must be unchanged: correct reads/writes, correct status=0, no unintended side effects beyond the intended cell.

threat_model: A malicious or buggy caller controls index (and possibly op, write_val) via the shared memory interface and can supply out-of-range values to read adjacent stack/heap/global memory (info leak) or write to adjacent memory (corruption), potentially reading or corrupting other kernels' state that share the same address space.
